newsitem.title: USA: GM will sell Hughes to Raytheon.
newsitem.headline: GM will sell Hughes to Raytheon.

text.p: General Motors Corp.'s Hughes Aircraft defense subsidiary will be sold to Raytheon Co. in a deal valued at $9.5 billion, the automaker announced Thursday.
The announcement made Raytheon the winner in a bidding war with Northrop Grumman Corp.
The purchase price consists of $5.1 billion in Raytheon stock and $4.4 billion in debt, Raytheon said.

The Hughes unit was a highly valued prize in the rapidly consolidating defence industry. A merged Raytheon-Hughes company will probably create the third largest U.S. defence contractor after the combination of Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp., which have agreed to merge, and Lockheed Martin Corp.

Hughes' defence operations produce missiles such as the Tomahawk cruise missile, radar systems and other defence electronics systems. Raytheon estimated combined annual revenues at about $21 billion and said the company would have 127,000 employees.
GM, which bought El Segundo, Calif.-based Hughes for about $5 billion in 1985, said it would move the unit's automotive electronics unit back into its Delphi Automotive Systems parts unit.
